state.case_summary:
A man in his 60s presented with crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections for the past 5 years. He denied hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss. No prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma were reported. He mentioned occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water.

Nasal endoscopy revealed destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, along with purulent, yellow drainage and crusting.

- Laboratory tests: C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, white blood cell count, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel results were normal. HIV test was negative.- Imaging studies:  Title: Computed Tomography on Initial Presentation  Description: Axial and coronal scans reveal a substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate. Shows thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses, erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system.- Chest CT:  Description: Showed enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum.- Pathology/Microbiology:  - Sinus mucosa showed noncaseating granulomas  - Initial AFB staining was negative  - Culture showed growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas  - AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node was positive  - Second FESS AFB PCR probe was positive

root.label: Chronic Progressive Sinusitis with Systemic and Pulmonary Involvement
supporting_facts: crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections for the past 5 years
destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates
enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum
positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node and second FESS
excluded_candidates: Bacterial sinusitis: reason ranked lower due to chronicity and systemic involvement
Fungal sinusitis: reason ranked lower due to lack of specific fungal elements in pathology
Vasculitis: reason ranked lower due to normal inflammatory markers and lack of specific vasculitic features
alarm_features: systemic involvement with enlarged lymph nodes
positive AFB PCR probe indicating possible tuberculosis
